name: Ceres
distance_note: Mean distance from the Sun (semi-major axis)
characteristics: Largest object in the main asteroid belt and the only dwarf planet in the inner Solar System. Visited by the Dawn spacecraft.
source: NASA Solar System Dynamics / JPL Small-Body Database, compiled from published values

name: Vesta
distance_note: Mean distance from the Sun (semi-major axis)
characteristics: Second most massive asteroid-belt object, a differentiated protoplanet with a large south-polar impact basin. Visited by the Dawn spacecraft.
source: NASA Solar System Dynamics / JPL Small-Body Database, compiled from published values

name: Eros
distance_note: Mean distance from the Sun (semi-major axis)
characteristics: Elongated near-Earth asteroid, about 17 km long. NEAR Shoemaker orbited it in 2000 and landed on its surface in 2001.
source: NASA Solar System Dynamics / JPL Small-Body Database, compiled from published values

name: Bennu
distance_note: Mean distance from the Sun (semi-major axis)
characteristics: Rubble-pile asteroid about half a kilometre across. OSIRIS-REx collected a sample and returned it to Earth in 2023.
source: NASA Solar System Dynamics / JPL Small-Body Database, compiled from published values

name: Ryugu
distance_note: Mean distance from the Sun (semi-major axis)
characteristics: Dark, top-shaped rubble-pile asteroid about 1 km across. Hayabusa2 returned samples to Earth in 2020.
source: NASA Solar System Dynamics / JPL Small-Body Database, compiled from published values

name: Halley's Comet
distance_note: Mean distance from the Sun (semi-major axis)
characteristics: Famous periodic comet with an orbital period of about 76 years, last at perihelion in 1986. Visited by several spacecraft in 1986.
discovery: Recorded since antiquity; periodicity shown by Edmond Halley, 1705
source: NASA Solar System Dynamics / JPL Small-Body Database, compiled from published values

name: 67P/Churyumov–Gerasimenko
distance_note: Mean distance from the Sun (semi-major axis)
characteristics: Jupiter-family comet with a bilobed nucleus about 4 km across. ESA's Rosetta orbited it and Philae landed on it in 2014.
source: NASA Solar System Dynamics / JPL Small-Body Database, compiled from published values
